goal: Finish the minimum reliable foundation of f(x) before starting real testing on the RimWorld mod. Autocommit already exists. Now focus on basic lesson structure, stable orchestrator + logging, simple HITL, and minimal git/phone control.

missing: Clean lesson folders and status lifecycle
Minimal status files and command mechanism for phone control

context.why_this_task: Need a stable and observable core before running real experiments on RimWorld. Advanced memory features (Activation Score, sleep, personal/shared memory, semantic search, Manager) are intentionally postponed until after the first real test runs.
constraints: Do NOT implement sleep / memory maintenance
Do NOT implement semantic search or embeddings
Prefer working and readable code over perfect architecture

plan.title: Basic Lesson Folder Structure + Minimal Lifecycle
plan.description: Replace any single-file lessons approach with a clean folder-based structure and simple status transitions.
concrete_tasks: Create directories if they do not exist: lessons/observations/, lessons/candidates/, lessons/promoted/, lessons/deprecated/
Define a minimal lesson schema (JSON). Required fields: id, status, rule, why, tags (list), created_at. Optional but useful: source, related_files, priority
Implement helper functions or methods: create_observation(...), move_to_candidate(id), move_to_promoted(id), move_to_deprecated(id)
Each lesson must be stored as a separate .json file inside the folder that matches its status
Lesson id format example: L-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<short_hash> or similar, must be unique
acceptance: Can create a new observation as a JSON file
Can move a lesson between statuses by changing folder + updating status field
No dependency on a single monolithic lessons file

plan.title: Stable Orchestrator Cycle + Logging
plan.description: Make the orchestrator robust enough for real runs and write clear logs.
concrete_tasks: Catch and handle common failures: invalid JSON from agents, empty responses, timeouts, unexpected exceptions
On failure: log the error, save what is possible, and either retry lightly or stop the cycle cleanly (do not crash the whole process silently)
Write logs to files (e.g. logs/orchestrator.log or logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log)
Each log entry should contain: timestamp, cycle number, agent name, event type, short message
Also log when files are changed by agents (at least which paths)
acceptance: Orchestrator survives typical LLM/parsing errors without full crash
Logs are written to disk and are human-readable
It is possible to understand from logs what happened in a cycle

plan.title: Basic HITL (Human-in-the-Loop)
plan.description: Force a pause after every N cycles and show a short summary to the human.
concrete_tasks: Add a configurable parameter (e.g. HITL_EVERY_N_CYCLES = 3)
After every N cycles the orchestrator stops and waits for human input
Generate a short summary containing: current goal, what was changed, key decisions or errors, list of new/updated lessons if any
Save the summary both to console and to status/last_summary.md
Accept simple human replies: continue / stop / note:<text>
Keep the interaction minimal and terminal-friendly
acceptance: Human can continue or stop the run
Summary is also written to status/last_summary.md

plan.title: Minimal Git-Cloud / Phone Control
plan.description: Allow monitoring and light control from a phone via git without a laptop.
concrete_tasks: Create and keep updated: status/current.md — short live status (what is running now, current step, last error if any)
Create and keep updated: status/last_summary.md — the latest HITL summary
Create folder commands/
Orchestrator periodically checks commands/ for new files
Supported simple commands (minimum): pause, continue, stop, note (content of the file = note text)
After a command is processed, move it to commands/done/ (with timestamp in filename if possible)
Do not build anything complex — only the minimum needed for remote monitoring and light control
acceptance: status/current.md exists and is updated during runs
status/last_summary.md is updated after HITL pauses
Dropping a simple command file into commands/ has an effect
Processed commands are moved to commands/done/

plan.title: Smoke Integration Check
plan.description: Verify that the foundation pieces work together before starting RimWorld work.
concrete_tasks: Run 1–2 short synthetic tasks through the orchestrator
Confirm that lessons can be created in the new folder structure
Confirm that logs are written
Confirm that HITL pause + summary works
Confirm that status files are updated
Confirm that a test command in commands/ is detected and processed
Fix only critical blockers found during this check
acceptance: A short end-to-end run completes without crashing
All four foundation pieces (lessons, logging, HITL, status/commands) show basic working behaviour

out_of_scope: Activation Score and the formula A = ...
Any RimWorld-specific code or mod logic
notes_for_agents: Researcher: Propose only the minimum necessary structure. Do not design advanced memory features in this task. Keep schemas small and clear.
Editor: Implement concrete, working code. Make each step finishable and testable. Prefer simple functions and explicit file operations.
Reviewer: Focus on reliability and simplicity. Reject over-engineering. Check that acceptance criteria of each step are actually met.
definition_of_done: lessons/observations, candidates, promoted (and optionally deprecated) folders exist and are used
A lesson can be created and moved between statuses as separate JSON files
Orchestrator handles common errors and writes readable logs to disk
HITL pause after N cycles works and writes status/last_summary.md
Simple commands via commands/ folder work and are moved to commands/done/
A short smoke test covering the above passes
